metadata.title: Nobody Is Awake At 3 AM
metadata.purpose: Provenance Gatekeeper Development Log, Week 12 — closing Phase 2 with Prometheus: a /metrics endpoint and custom counters, a pull-model scrape over the internal network, the PromQL that makes a counter mean something, and the gap between collecting metrics and being told.

metadata.series_note: Overlap check run across all 22 built reels. Week 5 (claude-gatekeeper-dashboard-stress) built an HTML dashboard over the SQLite ledger and argued HUMAN alert-fatigue — that argument is deliberately NOT repeated. This reel's added beat is mechanical: collection is not notification, and `up == 0` is the alert nobody writes. It also closes the loop opened in Week 4, whose incident rows nobody read.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Onkar Bhujbal. Last week Redis made the Provenance Gatekeeper fast. I know the cache works because I watched it work, in a terminal, with my own eyes — which is not a monitoring strategy, it is a habit. If the hallucination rate climbs at three in the morning, or Redis quietly stops hitting, nobody is staring at that terminal. This week closes Phase 2 with Prometheus and real metrics.

beats.narration_text: Exposing metrics is the easy half. The half that decides whether any of this matters is whether something is configured to shout when the numbers go wrong, while I am asleep.

props.text:
Collecting is the work.
A graph cannot wake you.

beats.authoring_note: Both readings are true sentences: 'Collecting is the work.' and, corrected, 'Alerting is the work.' — the swap is the reel's thesis, and the second line holds for either.

beats.narration_text: Giving the service a pulse took very little code. The Prometheus FastAPI instrumentator wires into the app and exposes a slash-metrics endpoint, which gets you request counts and latency histograms for free. The part worth more than the free part is underneath: custom counters for the things only this system knows — every cache hit, every miss, and every blocked claim, labelled by variance type.
beats.new_visual_element: The pulse, in a dozen lines

show.event: code card opens on a hard cut; traffic-light dot arms terracotta
the instrumentator line reveals — HTTP metrics for free
the custom counters reveal — the domain-specific half
the closing note lands: the label set is a design decision

props.title: app/main.py
props.code:
Instrumentator().instrument(app).expose(app)
#   -> GET /metrics : counts + latency

CLAIMS_EVALUATED = Counter(
    "gatekeeper_claims_evaluated_total",
    "claims seen", ["verdict", "variance_type"],
)
CACHE_EVENTS = Counter(
    "gatekeeper_cache_events_total",
    "redis outcomes", ["result"],   # hit | miss
)

# Labels are a schema. Keep them small,
# and never label by claim_id.
props.sparkLine: Free metrics, then the ones that matter.

beats.honesty_note: Reconstructed from the counters the script names (CLAIMS_EVALUATED, CACHE_EVENTS) and the Instrumentator line it quotes. The low-cardinality warning is the reel's addition — labelling by claim_id would create one series per claim and is the standard way to take down a Prometheus.

beats.narration_text: Prometheus does not wait to be told. Unlike the webhook we built in Week nine, which pushes, Prometheus pulls: a container in the same Compose stack reaches across the internal Docker network every five seconds, reads slash-metrics, and writes the snapshot into its time-series database. One useful consequence — if the Gatekeeper goes down, the scrape fails, and that failure is itself a metric you can alert on.

beats.narration_text: Now I can ask questions instead of reading logs. One correction worth making, because it is the most common mistake with Prometheus: a counter only ever goes up. Graph claims-evaluated-total directly and you get a line that rises forever, which tells you nothing. You almost always want a rate over a window — and for the cache, a ratio of two rates. That is the difference between a chart that looks busy and a number you could actually alert on.
beats.new_visual_element: The query that looks right and is useless

show.event: left panel lands: the raw counter query
on 'rises forever', the monotonic series highlights terracotta IN PLACE
note lands beneath: it has never once gone down
right panel reveals the rate and the ratio
ink stamp lands: RATE, NOT TOTAL

props.sparkLine: Both of these are valid PromQL.
props.hotNote: a counter only rises — this line cannot show you a problem
props.code:
# claims per second, last 5 min
rate(
  gatekeeper_claims_evaluated_total[5m]
)

# cache hit ratio
sum(rate(cache_events_total{result="hit"}[5m]))
/
sum(rate(cache_events_total[5m]))
props.stampSub: a counter answers 'how many ever' — you asked 'what is happening now'

beats.honesty_note: CORRECTION to the supplied script, which shows `gatekeeper_claims_evaluated_total` rendering 'a clean line graph' of intercepts and hit-vs-miss. Graphed raw, a counter is monotonically increasing and shows neither. The counter values shown are illustrative.

beats.narration_text: And here is what I have actually built, stated honestly. I can now answer the three A.M. question — in the morning, when I open the dashboard. Nothing yet wakes anyone. A metric sitting in a time-series database that no one queries is the same shape of failure as the incident rows I wrote to SQLite back in Week four: recorded, retrievable, and unread. Worse, if the Gatekeeper dies the graph simply stops, and a stopped graph looks calm. Until there are alerting rules — including one on the scrape itself — this is a better memory, not a better response.

beats.authoring_note: BEAT ADDED. The script's hook promises to solve the 3 AM problem and its Scene 4 delivers a dashboard, which does not. This states the gap plainly and ties it to Week 4's unread SQLite rows — the same failure in a nicer database. Deliberately NOT the human-fatigue argument from Week 5's reel: the point here is that no notification path exists at all yet.

beats.narration_text: So: you cannot optimise what you cannot measure — expose your metrics and stop flying blind. Then write the rules, because a number nobody is told about is just a tidier way of not knowing.

props.title: alerts.yml
props.code:
- alert: InterceptRateSpike
  expr: rate(claims{verdict="blocked"}[10m])
      > 3 * rate(claims{verdict="blocked"}[6h])
  for: 10m

- alert: GatekeeperDown
  expr: up{job="gatekeeper"} == 0
  for: 2m

# TASK: measure everything that matters.
# Then route it to something that rings.
props.sparkLine: A number nobody is told is not monitoring.

beats.honesty_note: These rules are the recommended next step, not shipped configuration — the reel is explicit in B05 that alerting does not exist yet.

beats.narration_text: Here is the prompt worth running against your own stack. Ask a model to trace the full path from a metric crossing a threshold to a human being interrupted, and to name every step that does not exist yet. For most projects that path stops at the dashboard, and the dashboard is not a step — it is a place you have to already be looking.
